findings.root_cause: Refined root cause (parent confirmed). Memory 0.6.0 re-delivers the IDENTICAL MemoryAnalysisRequest only on lease reclaim / authority-transient retry of the same batch; every executor failure creates a new batch whose request_hash, attempt, job_id and idempotency_key all change while the evidence set stays the same (or grows). A Host ledger keyed only by (request_hash, attempt) therefore (a) correctly dedups reclaim/authority retries, but (b) cannot see a prior `sent_unknown` when Memory retries with attempt+1 -> blind resend of the same evidence set, violating ASSET-PROVIDER-IDEMPOTENCY. Second facet: with a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat/completions endpoint the provider response id is only known once the response arrived, the Host reconciliation adapter is a constant STILL_UNKNOWN and the SDK never replays, so `sent_unknown -> sent_confirmed` has NO executable production path; AC-2 (3)'s 'unknown then confirmed by provider response id' branch is exercisable only through an injected test reconciliation observer. Third facet: the plan's 30 s Memory lease is shorter than real analysis latency, so 0.6.0 will reclaim and re-deliver a request while the Host's provider call is still in flight; only a Host durable `handed_off` row (refuse/await, never re-dispatch) prevents a concurrent duplicate call. EXECUTABLE DESIGN the plan must state: (1) ledger table post_turn_invocation_attempts UNIQUE(request_hash, attempt) PLUS attempt-independent evidence_set_key = sha256(canonical(request.to_json() minus {job_id, attempt, idempotency_key})) PLUS a member index (subject, run_id, evidence_id, attempt_row_id) because membership grows between retries (probe P2); pre-dispatch rule: any member evidence with an open handed_off/sent_unknown row -> refuse without provider call. (2) Classification reuses Host dispatch handoff facts: transport not entered / ConnectTimeout -> not_sent (resend allowed as attempt+1); anything after handoff without a parsed response -> sent_unknown; parsed response persisted in the SAME transaction as state=succeeded together with provider_response_id/provider_response_hash (so there is no window in which a response exists but is not durable). (3) Terminal state of sent_unknown for this provider = Host executor raises a definite AnalysisAttemptBlocked(sent_unknown_unresolved) on every re-delivery (0 provider calls); Memory burns its retry schedule and dead-letters with last_error_code=analysis_executor_failed (probe P1b/P4); Host writes a durable event memory.analysis.blocked{reason, evidence_set_key} so the user-visible reason is not lost behind Memory's coarse code; raw evidence untouched (outbox row dead_letter, evidence_envelopes intact). Optional 0.6.1 addition (same wheel as Task 5): AnalysisExecutorPermanentError -> immediate dead_letter carrying the Host reason instead of N retries and N failed batch rows. (4) Confirm branch: keep `sent_confirmed` reachable only via an injected ProviderReconciliationObservation(COMPLETED) in the deterministic S5B-S3 lane; document that production has no confirm path. (5) lease_seconds must be >= analysis_budget.deadline_ms/1000 + provider timeout margin (e.g. 120 s), and the Host ledger must treat a re-delivery of a row in handed_off as 'await/refuse', never as a fresh dispatch.

findings.root_cause: Confirmed. In 0.6.0 the audited request lineage is a worker constant while the Host executor must dial the originating Run's binding; the two diverge the moment the user changes provider/model, and there is no claim-side filter, so 'one worker per binding fingerprint' is NOT workable (workers race on the same FIFO batch; the wrong-config worker burns attempts) and 'config from the batch's originating run binding' is impossible because config is fixed before the claim reveals the batch (peeking Memory's jobs table is raw SQL, not a port). WORKABLE COMPOSITION: (A) Memory 0.6.1 (Task 5, same wheel already planned): bind lineage at ingest -- ingest_committed_evidence(envelope, receipt, *, analysis_lineage=AnalysisLineage(provider_id, model_id, model_config_hash)) persisted per evidence row; claim_analysis_batch derives request.provider_id/model_id/model_config_hash from the members (assert uniform, mirroring the run_id/disclosure 'analysis batch authority differs' check) and MemoryJobWorkerConfig keeps only prompt/schema/policy/validator/budget/lease fields (or keeps provider fields as non-authoritative defaults). Host: model_config_hash = sha256(canonical{provider_id, provider_incarnation_id, provider_config_revision, model_id, model_params, endpoint_identity}) computed from the durable SdkRunBindingV1 at terminal commit (same transaction as the ingestion outbox row) and passed through the outbox worker to ingest; the executor rebuilds the adapter from foreground_run_sdk_bindings and REFUSES (definite failure, 0 provider calls) when request lineage != rebuilt binding hash. Audit consequence: Memory llm_invocations and the Host attempt ledger carry the same true provider/model/config hash + binding_fingerprint -> contract 96-97 satisfied and cross-checkable. (B) 0.6.0-only interim for the Task 4 milestone: single worker whose config mirrors the CURRENT provider binding; executor verifies request lineage == H(binding of request.run_id); jobs from Runs bound to a different provider/model are blocked (0 provider calls) and dead-letter after max_attempts -- acceptable only as the explicitly documented milestone interim, because it silently loses memory formation for pre-switch turns. Plan edits: Task 4 (5) must say 'interim B on 0.6.0'; Task 5 must add the lineage-at-ingest API + uniform-lineage assert + tests; S5B-S1 root run on 0.6.1 must assert llm_invocations.provider_id/model_id == originating Run binding.

Memory 0.6.1 scope grows by two items from this cluster: analysis lineage bound at ingest (new ingest kwarg + evidence column + claim derivation + uniform-lineage assert) and an optional AnalysisExecutorPermanentError; both change the wheel hash and the v7 schema and must be in the same cutover receipt as materialization/owner registration.

The Task 4 milestone on 0.6.0 can only run with the interim composition (single worker config mirroring the current binding, executor verifying lineage); the milestone declaration must say so, and the 0.6.1 root run must re-assert Run-bound lineage in llm_invocations.

conclusion.summary: Both P1 parents confirmed on the real 0.6.0 wheel and refined into executable designs. Probe facts: Memory re-delivers the identical request only on lease reclaim / authority-transient retry (same batch_id, request_hash, attempt); every executor failure creates a new batch with new request_hash/attempt/job_id/idempotency_key while the evidence set is unchanged or grows; crash-after-result-commit needs no executor call at all (Memory retains the envelope). Hence the Host ledger must be keyed by (request_hash, attempt) AND an attempt-independent evidence_set_key with a per-member evidence index; sent_unknown has no production confirm path for a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoint (response id exists only with a response; Host reconciliation adapter is constant STILL_UNKNOWN; SDK never replays), so its executable terminal is 'refuse every re-delivery with 0 provider calls -> Memory dead_letter (analysis_executor_failed) + Host durable blocked event', with sent_confirmed exercisable only via an injected test observer; the 30 s lease is shorter than measured analysis latency and must be raised above the analysis deadline. Lineage: 0.6.0 audits worker constants and claim has no config filter, so per-binding workers cannot work; the workable composition is Memory 0.6.1 lineage-bound-at-ingest (Host passes binding-derived model_config_hash in the terminal-commit outbox row; executor verifies request lineage == rebuilt binding, else blocked) with a documented 0.6.0 interim for the milestone. Binding-unrebuildable terminal: bounded retries -> dead_letter with Host-visible reason, raw evidence retained, restart does not trigger it (incarnation_id is persisted). No further spike required; plan edits to Task 4 (5), Task 5, S5B-S3 lane and the non-functional lease bound are needed before closure.
